lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Care and Basic Food Safety
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: simple no-heat preparation

objective: Given a short list of ingredients, learners independently plan and assemble one simple, no-heat food item (such as a sandwich, a fruit bowl, or a wrap) that meets three stated criteria, without adult step-by-step direction.
scenario: Without being told the exact steps, the learner is given (or selects) a short list of no-heat ingredients and independently plans and assembles one finished food item that meets three criteria: uses at least three ingredients, is assembled in a logical order, and is served in a way that's ready to eat.
safetyNotes: No heat source is used in this lesson by design; any knife used for soft, no-heat ingredients is adult-approved beforehand.

simulationAlternative.description: If the specific ingredients aren't available at home, the learner instead plans the full sequence in writing for a no-heat food item using ingredients they do have or a provided list, describing each assembly step in the order they would do it, in place of physically assembling it.

materials: a knife appropriate for the ingredients (adult-approved if needed)

tasks.directions: Quickly recall: name two no-heat foods you already know how to put together without help.
Plan and assemble one no-heat food item using at least three ingredients, in a logical order, served ready to eat.

prompts.text: List the ingredients you used and the order you assembled them in.
My finished item uses at least three ingredients.
My finished item is served in a way that's actually ready to eat (not still in pieces on the counter).

tasks.directions: Rate your no-heat-preparation confidence and pick what comes next.

prompts.text: Rate your confidence in assembling a no-heat food item on your own (very / somewhat / not yet), cite one specific step from today as evidence, and choose: ready to try a food item with more steps, ready to review this again, or need a different explanation.

remediation: If the assembly order is illogical (for example adding a topping before a base that needs to be prepared), reteach by having the learner narrate their planned order out loud before starting, catching sequencing problems before they touch any ingredients.
extension: Plan and assemble a second no-heat food item that meets a new constraint (uses one ingredient the learner has never used before, or serves two people instead of one).
